title: Reading the structure as a working system

blocks.heading: Reading the structure as a working system
blocks.text: The features of a structure interact. Adding supervisors can narrow a manager’s direct span and provide closer support, but it can also add a level to the chain of command. Removing levels may speed formal communication while widening the remaining managers’ spans. Delegation can relieve a bottleneck by authorising a subordinate to decide, but responsibility, resources and limits must be clear. A manager cannot meaningfully expect someone to resolve customer complaints while denying authority to offer any remedy. Central control can preserve consistency for high-risk or expensive decisions; local discretion can improve response where staff understand customers and have the necessary competence. Judge these effects in context because neither a tall nor a flat structure has a guaranteed performance advantage. An organisation chart shows the formal structure, not informal friendships or how well people cooperate.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Ulima Furniture requires the owner’s approval for every small replacement part, even though the workshop head knows the repair work. The owner becomes a decision bottleneck. Delegating purchases up to an agreed limit can let the head obtain parts sooner; the owner should monitor spending and retain oversight. Removing the spending limit entirely would create a different risk from authorising routine repairs.
